name: Titan live control latency (atlas Experiment 3 step 2)
status: PROPOSAL — NOT APPROVED. Device read/write of one live control; no flash.
purpose: A host-timed trigger (a riser puppet now, a release puppet later) is only usable if a command reaches the device quickly and consistently. This measures command to device readback.
operation: Twenty live speed changes on board 0 through the mixer API (POST /api/controls with the session token), alternating 0.50 and 0.55. Each is confirmed when /api/status board_states.0.speed equals the commanded value; the status is polled every 5 ms. Board 1 is never commanded.
latency: Wall-clock time from just before the POST to the first status read showing the commanded value on board 0.
pass: all 20 commands are confirmed within 2.0 s
board 1 speed reads 0.50 at every poll
after the run board 0 speed is restored to 0.50 and confirmed
jitter_reported: p50, p95, max and (p95 - p50) are reported; a host-timed trigger can lead by p50 but carries (p95 - p50) as timing uncertainty.

planted_faults.late_poll: The same run scored with 200 ms added to every latency (a poll that starts 200 ms late). Expected RED on the p95 clause.
planted_faults.board1_command: One extra command scored as if it were on board 1 (board 1 speed 0.55 in its readback). Expected RED on the board-1 clause.

safety: Speed only. Brightness, palette and mode are not touched. The Titan keeps visualising throughout; testing-scope ruling applies.
